newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lockheed possible project partner - DASA.
newsitem.headline: Lockheed possible project partner - DASA.

text.p: German aerospace concern Daimler-Benz Aerospace (DASA) said on Saturday that Lockheed Martin Corp of the United States was a possible partner for Airbus projects.

But it made no comment on a report in the London Times that Lockheed and the Airbus consortium, which groups DASA, British Aerospace, France's Aerospatiale and Spain's CASA, were discussing a possible merger.
"I don't know anything about that," a DASA spokesman said in response to an enquiry. But he said Lockheed was a possible partner for discussions on individual projects.
A full merger would almost certainly be impossible anyway before Airbus converts from a multinational consortium to a single company in 1999.

But DASA chief executive Manfred Bischoff said earlier this year that Airbus was interested in finding a partner to help it develop the planned 800-seater A3XX "superjumbo", and that Lockheed could be such a partner.

The Times said the two groups were poised to announce agreements on some major aerospace projects before attempting a corporate link-up. It said Lockheed was set to become a risk-sharing partner in the superjumbo.
